title: Qsyn A Developer-Friendly Quantum Circuit Synthesis Framework for NISQ Era and Beyond

predicted_errors.error_location: Table I / immediately following the paragraph beginning “We compare Qsyn’s efficiency and optimization power with PyZX”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text repeatedly cites “Table I” as containing runtime, memory, RZ-count, and circuit-depth results, but the supplied paper contains only the table title (“COMPARISON WITH PYZX [1] ON THE GATE-LEVEL SYNTHESIS STAGE”) and unit labels. No table body, benchmark rows, numerical values, hardware specification, or limits are provided. Thus the reported comparison cannot be inspected or verified.

The abstract claims that Qsyn’s “superior performance” is demonstrated through “fair comparisons with PyZX,” while the results paragraph claims shorter runtimes, lower memory usage, smaller/equal RZ counts, and average shallower circuits. The document supplies no underlying Table I data or aggregate calculation, so these comparative and superiority conclusions are unsupported by the presented evidence.

predicted_errors.error_location: PyZX comparison experiment / purported Table I
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The comparison reports runtime, memory, and TLE/MLE outcomes but provides none of the information needed for a reproducible or fair performance comparison: PyZX/Qsyn versions or commits, PyZX command/configuration, benchmark source and exact inputs, machine/OS/CPU/RAM, timeout and memory-limit values, repetition protocol, or definition of the synthesis/optimization objective. Consequently, statements such as “PyZX encounters TLE and/or MLE” and that Qsyn is faster/lower-memory cannot be evaluated as a controlled experiment.

The supplied full text uses citations “[1]” for PyZX and “[11]” for the claimed compact MCT ZX-diagram representation and early-stopping strategy, but contains no references/bibliography. The cited sources therefore cannot be identified or checked, and the claimed attribution to [11] is unverifiable.
